title: Choose a small, real practice project
summary: The best proof that you can do the job is to do part of it. Pick a small, real problem you can study with real people, and set a clear scope so that you finish.

beginner: List problems you or people around you have: a local club's sign-up process, a charity's website, a tool you use at work (using public information only) or a feature in an app you use.
Choose one where you can reach at least five real users within a couple of weeks, and where the problem is real, not invented.
If the project touches your work, check that you will not use anything confidential, and do not name colleagues or clients. If in doubt, choose something outside work.

Write a one-paragraph brief: who has the problem, what you think it is, what you will produce (for example five interviews, a one-page brief, a ranked list of ideas and a measure of success) and the date you will finish.
Time-box it to four to six weeks at a few hours a week. A smaller project that you finish beats a big one you drop.
Tell one person what you are doing and ask them to check in on you.

toolExamples.notion: Keep the brief, the timeline and a list of participants on one page.

definitionOfDone: A one-paragraph brief with scope and an end date
A person who will check in on your progress
pitfalls: Choosing a huge product you can't learn anything real about
Making up users instead of finding them
